You are a strict evaluator of answers produced by a document question-answering system. You are given a question, a reference answer written by a human from the source document, the answer the system gave, and the exact context the system was shown. Judge only what is written. Use no outside knowledge.

Produce four judgements.

1. correctness: compare the system answer with the reference answer.
   - "correct": it states the same essential facts, numbers and conditions as the reference. Extra detail is fine if it does not contradict the reference.
   - "partial": it states some but not all of the essential facts, or is right but imprecise on a key number or condition.
   - "incorrect": it contradicts the reference, gives a wrong key fact, gives no answer, or declines to answer.
   For a question marked UNANSWERABLE the reference answer says the information is not in the documents. There the answer is "correct" only if the system declines to answer or says the information is not available; any substantive answer is "incorrect".

2. is_refusal: true if the system answer declines to answer or says the information is not available in the document, false otherwise. A partial answer that also notes some missing detail is not a refusal.

3. claims: break the system answer into its independent factual claims (at most 10; merge trivial ones). For each, mark supported true only if the CONTEXT states it or directly implies it. A claim that is true in the real world but absent from the context is unsupported. Compare against the context, never against the reference answer. If the answer is a refusal, return an empty list.

4. correctness_reason: one sentence, at most 30 words.

Respond with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"correctness": "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect", "correctness_reason": "...", "is_refusal": true | false, "claims": [{"claim": "...", "supported": true | false}]}

Question:
What share of net assets can a fund hold in short term deposits with one bank, and may the AMC charge management fees on such parking for liquid and debt schemes?

Reference answer:
At most 10% with any one scheduled commercial bank including its subsidiaries; no investment management or advisory fees may be charged for such parking.

System answer:
A fund may park no more than 10% of its net assets in short‑term deposits with any single scheduled commercial bank. For liquid and debt‑oriented schemes, the AMC is not allowed to charge any investment management or advisory fees for such parking.

12.9.1.1 “Short Term” for parking of funds by Mutual Funds shall be treated as

12.9.1.2 Such deposits shall be held in the name of the concerned scheme. 
 
12.9.1.3 Mutual Funds shall not park more than 15% of their net assets in 
short term deposits of all scheduled commercial banks put together. 
This limit however may be raised to 20% with prior approval of the 
Trustees. Also, parking of funds in short term deposits of associate 
and sponsor scheduled commercial banks together shall not exceed 
20% of the total deployment by the Mutual Fund in short term 
deposits. 
 
12.9.1.4 Mutual Funds shall not park more than 10% of the net assets in short 
term deposits with any one scheduled commercial bank including its 
subsidiaries.

a. Investment restrictions specified in Schedule Seven of the Mutual 
Funds Regulations are applicable to overseas investments stipulated 
under paragraph 12.11.2.1- 12.11.2.9 
 
b. However, Clause 4 of the Seventh Schedule of the Mutual Funds 
Regulations that restricts investments in Mutual Fund units up to 5% 
of net assets and prohibits charging of fees, shall not be applicable to 
investments in Mutual Funds in foreign countries made in accordance 
with these Guidelines. 
 
c. Management fees and other expenses charged by the Mutual Funds in 
foreign countries along with the management fee and recurring 
expenses charged to the domestic Mutual Fund scheme shall not 
exceed the total limits on expenses as prescribed under Regulation 
52(6) of the Mutual Funds Regulations. Where the scheme is investing 
only a part of the net assets in overseas Mutual Funds, the same 
principle shall be applicable for that part of investment. Details of 
calculation for charging such expenses shall be reported to the Board 
of the AMC and the Trustees and shall also be disclosed in the Annual 
Report of the scheme

securities, ADR/GDR/overseas ETF(s) shall be made in advance of 
making investments. On receipt of approval from the Board, 
intimation may be sent by the AMC(s) to Overseas Investment 
Division, Foreign Exchange Department, RBI.
